common_name: Fry Seedless Muscadine Grape (Seedless Sport of Classic Fry)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in late winter to early spring on a sturdy trellis in full sun, well-drained soil; self-fertile, unlike the seeded parent Fry variety, so a single vine can produce fruit.

directions: Plant on a sturdy trellis or arbor in well-drained soil in full sun. Fry Seedless is a seedless sport of the classic bronze Fry muscadine, retaining the same large size and sweet, richly flavored fruit that made the original Fry a Southern favorite, but without the large seeds most muscadines carry, making it more convenient for fresh eating. As is typical of seedless muscadine selections, individual berries run somewhat smaller than the seeded parent variety, a common tradeoff in muscadine breeding, but the flavor and eating quality remain excellent. Unlike seeded Fry, which requires a separate pollinizer, Fry Seedless is self-fertile, simplifying planting for gardeners who want just one or two vines. Harvest as berries fully color and detach easily with a gentle tug, typically over an extended late-summer season.

common_name: Black Fry Muscadine Grape (Dark-Skinned Sport of Classic Fry)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in late winter to early spring on a sturdy trellis in full sun, well-drained soil; not self-fertile and requires a self-fertile pollinizer variety such as Carlos or Cowart nearby for fruit set.

directions: Plant on a sturdy trellis or arbor in well-drained soil in full sun, with a compatible self-fertile pollinizer variety nearby. Black Fry is a dark-skinned sport of the classic bronze Fry muscadine, retaining the same large fruit size and sweet flavor as its well-known parent while offering the deep black-purple skin some growers and markets specifically prefer over the bronze color. As with the original Fry, individual berries are notably large for a muscadine, and the vine is a strong, productive grower once established. Because it is not self-fertile, ensure a compatible pollinizer variety is planted within pollination range, and harvest as berries fully darken and detach easily with a gentle tug over an extended late-summer harvest window.

Hall is a self-fertile bronze muscadine producing medium to large, sweet, flavorful fruit on a vigorous, productive vine with good disease resistance, making it a practical, low-fuss choice for home gardeners who want reliable production from a single vine without needing to plant a separate pollinizer. The self-fertile trait, shared by a growing number of modern muscadine releases, has made varieties like Hall increasingly popular for smaller home gardens where space for multiple vines is limited. Harvest as berries fully color and detach easily from the stem with a gentle tug, typically over an extended ripening window from late summer into early fall.

common_name: Sugargloss Muscadine Grape (Glossy Sweet Bronze-Pink Muscadine)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in late winter to early spring on a sturdy trellis in full sun, well-drained soil; check pollination requirements before planting a single vine, since some muscadine selections are not self-fertile.

directions: Plant on a sturdy trellis or arbor in well-drained soil in full sun. Sugargloss produces bronze to pinkish-bronze muscadine fruit with a distinctively glossy skin and an unusually high sugar content, making it one of the sweeter muscadine selections available, well suited to fresh eating for gardeners who prioritize sweetness over the more traditionally tart-edged muscadine flavor. The vine is a solid, productive grower under standard Southern muscadine growing conditions. Harvest as berries fully color, develop their characteristic glossy sheen, and detach easily from the stem with a gentle tug, typically over an extended late-summer to early-fall ripening window characteristic of muscadine grapes.

common_name: Early Fry Muscadine Grape (Early-Ripening Sport of Classic Fry)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in late winter to early spring on a sturdy trellis in full sun, well-drained soil; not self-fertile and requires a self-fertile pollinizer variety such as Carlos or Cowart nearby for fruit set.

directions: Plant on a sturdy trellis or arbor in well-drained soil in full sun, with a compatible self-fertile pollinizer variety nearby. Early Fry is a sport of the classic bronze Fry muscadine selected specifically for ripening earlier in the season than the standard variety, giving growers a jump on the muscadine harvest while retaining the same large fruit size and rich, sweet flavor that made the original Fry so popular across the South. The earlier ripening window can also help the crop finish before the heaviest late-summer pest and disease pressure builds, a practical advantage in humid Gulf Coast growing conditions. Harvest as berries fully color and detach easily from the stem with a gentle tug, and expect the harvest window to open somewhat ahead of standard Fry plantings.
